criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the MAE carve-outs for conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry and changes in Environmental Laws lack a disproportionate-impact exception. It proposes adding a qualifier so those matters remain relevant to the extent they disproportionately affect the Company relative to industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed MAE definition adds an explicit disproportionate-impact proviso covering clauses (i) through (vi), including the industry-specific and Environmental Law/regulatory carve-outs, relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes full proposed replacement contract language for the Material Adverse Effect definition in Section 1.01, including an express disproportionate-impact exception applicable to clauses (i) through (vi).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly ties the concern to Target’s environmental remediation, hazardous-waste, permit, and government-contract business, explaining that industry-wide or Environmental Law developments could materially and disproportionately harm Target. It also states that the seller’s carve-outs could insulate such target-specific regulatory harm, adequately explaining why the carve-outs are especially problematic for this environmental services company.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Section 6.01's interim operating covenants lack a specific restriction on transactions with Seller or Seller affiliates and proposes a new consent-based covenant covering entry into, amendment, renewal, termination, payment under, or acceleration of affiliate arrangements between signing and closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.01(b)(xiv), which prohibits the Company from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, or terminating transactions or agreements with Seller or Seller affiliates without Buyer's prior written consent, subject to limited specified exceptions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: The affiliate-transactions covenant rationale expressly cites “$1.6 million of above-market annual rent under the Affiliate Lease” as a diligence concern supporting the specific consent right over affiliate arrangements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft uses a 20% cap ($43,000,000) and contrasts it with the term sheet's agreed 12.5% cap ($26,875,000), including proposed replacement language.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing the 20% / $43,000,000 indemnification cap with 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, equal to $26,875,000.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites “Executed Term Sheet §8” as a source for the cap correction and states that the executed term sheet fixes the general indemnification cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value ($26.875 million). It also identifies the executed term sheet as dated September 10, 2025.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller's uniform 12-month survival period as inadequate for environmental representations, including Section 4.15 Environmental Matters and Environmental Permits, and proposes extending survival to 36 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that Environmental Representations survive until 36 months after Closing in revised Section 9.01(c), and also reserves the option to seek survival through the full applicable statute of limitations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly ties the proposed 36-month survival period for environmental representations to the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure and the active Hargrove remediation project, noting that Dalton Creek liability may take years to crystallize and Hargrove has an 18–24 month remaining timeline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes its restriction that Buyer cannot obtain indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies of which Buyer or its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly deletes the anti-sandbagging provision and replaces it with a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer's indemnification rights are not affected, defeated, or diminished by any investigation or knowledge obtained before or after Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in the replacement Section 9.06, stating that indemnification and other remedies are not affected by Buyer's investigation, knowledge, notice, or available information.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Dalton Creek EPA CERCLA §104(e) matter as requiring a separate Special Indemnity. It proposes a dedicated Section 9.02(e) with 72-month survival, first-dollar recovery, no basket or general cap, and 36 months of escrow support, distinct from general environmental representation indemnification.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity survives until 72 months following the Closing Date, including in the proposed Section 9.02(e).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity is first-dollar and “shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap,” and it also proposes conforming language excluding it from the basket and general cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity rationale that the diligence memo estimates exposure at $1.5 million to $6 million, using that range to justify the proposed special indemnity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05(d)'s requirement to operate consistently with past practice and in good faith to maximize the earnout as overly restrictive, explaining that it would constrain Buyer's integration, restructuring, personnel, and capital-allocation decisions. It proposes replacing that covenant with a narrow prohibition on actions taken primarily to avoid or reduce the earnout.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller’s affirmative past-practice and earnout-maximization obligations with a narrow covenant prohibiting actions taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the earnout. It also states that Buyer has no affirmative obligation to operate in any particular manner or maximize the earnout.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout commentary expressly explains that the seller’s affirmative operating covenants could constrain Buyer’s platform integration, restructuring, personnel decisions, capital allocation, and bolt-on strategy, and states that the proposed language restores Buyer’s post-closing operational flexibility.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the draft permits repayment “at or promptly following the Closing” and omits payoff letters from Seller’s closing deliverables and Buyer’s closing conditions. It proposes requiring executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness at least three business days before Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly requires executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness no later than three Business Days before Closing. It also requires each letter to include wire transfer instructions and provide for lien releases, including UCC-3 termination statements and other lien-release instruments.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller’s “at or promptly following” mechanic with a requirement that all Closing Indebtedness be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full at Closing through the closing funds flow. It also requires a funds flow agreement covering repayment of all Closing Indebtedness.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes adding Section 7.02(h) as a Buyer closing condition requiring Seller to deliver the payoff letters specified in Section 2.03(d), and also adds them as closing deliverables under Section 2.08(a)(x).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft lacks specific government-contract anti-assignment, novation, and recognition provisions for the Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management contracts. It also proposes representations and covenants addressing the Anti-Assignment Act, FAR Part 42.12, novation/recognition submissions, agency notices, and post-closing cooperation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum identifies all four active government contracts by agency and specifically states that the two federal contracts—U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Land Management—may require novation or recognition under FAR 42.1204.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes a specific pre-closing covenant in new Section 6.05A requiring Seller and the Company to notify relevant agencies, submit required government contract novation or recognition requests, and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the agreements. It also proposes a related closing condition addressing those submissions and adverse agency indications.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12 as legal bases for government-contract novation, recognition, and related notice requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft lacks a pre- or post-closing covenant addressing environmental permit change-of-control notifications, approvals, transfers, or re-issuances. It proposes new Section 6.05B requiring pre-closing identification and submissions, commercially reasonable efforts to obtain approvals, and post-closing cooperation for pending permit transfers, re-issuances, amendments, and approvals.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.05B, requiring Seller to assist before Closing with identifying and submitting required environmental permit notifications, applications, and approval requests, and to provide post-Closing cooperation for permit transfers, reissuances, amendments, and approvals.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that environmental permits in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada may require change-of-control notification or approval even though the transaction is structured as a stock purchase and the permit-holding entity remains unchanged.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft contains no provision addressing Buyer's R&W insurance policy or waiver of the insurer's subrogation rights against Seller and its affiliates, and proposes a new Section 10.13 to add that waiver subject to a fraud exception.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 10.13 requiring the R&W insurer to waive subrogation and other recovery rights against Seller and related parties, with an express exception for claims arising from or relating to actual fraud by Seller.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Buyer is obtaining/placing an R&W Insurance policy, identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters, and connects the policy to the need for an insurer subrogation waiver in favor of Seller and its affiliates, except for Seller fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft imposes a five-year non-compete while the term sheet agreed to a three-year period, and proposes replacing the duration with three years.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft applies nationwide and states that the term sheet limits the non-compete geography to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. It also proposes replacement language using only those four states.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the draft restricts Seller from engaging in “any business,” while the term sheet limits the restricted activities to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services. It also proposes replacement language conforming to that narrower scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the non-compete period from five years to three years following the Closing Date, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) limits the non-compete to environmental remediation or hazardous waste management businesses in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the restricted business activities to the provision of “environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services,” matching the term sheet’s required scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the five-year nationwide restriction covering “any business” would sweep in Evergreen’s unrelated construction and timber operations and raises enforceability concerns. It also proposes carve-outs preserving those legitimate businesses.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The indemnification cap discrepancy (20% / $43 million versus 12.5% / $26.875 million) is expressly rated HIGH in both the Priority Matrix and the detailed Section 1.01 discussion.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06 (sandbagging) is expressly assigned CRITICAL priority in both the Priority Matrix and the detailed markup, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a separate “Items Intentionally Left Unchanged” section identifying several acceptable provisions and briefly explaining why, including the 1% true-deductible basket, actual-knowledge qualifier, 10-business-day good-standing certificate timing, and Delaware governing law.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly flags multiple issues for further partner/client discussion before finalizing positions. Examples include whether completed government-contract novations should be a closing condition, whether environmental representations should survive for the full statute of limitations, the dedicated Dalton Creek escrow allocation, and whether to narrow the non-solicit. It also includes a dedicated “Negotiation Roadmap and Open Decisions” section.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly references the escrow as $16.125 million in the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity implementation note. This equals 7.5% of the $215 million base enterprise value, and no conflicting escrow amount is stated.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides that the escrow portion designated for the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity remains available until 36 months after closing, distinct from the general 18-month escrow release. It also conforms Section 9.08 to retain Special Indemnity reserves for that 36-month period.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion expressly states that the economic thresholds are correct, including a "$25 million maximum," which correctly references the maximum earnout payment as $25,000,000.

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion expressly states that the full-payment Adjusted EBITDA threshold is $38 million, which correctly corresponds to $38,000,000.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion expressly states that the economic thresholds are correct, including a $32 million floor, a $38 million full-payment threshold, and linear interpolation between them, which reflects pro-rata payment between the floor and threshold.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer's M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE disproportionate-impact qualifier, earnout operating covenant, indemnification cap, environmental survival, pro-sandbagging, debt payoff mechanics, government-contract novation, permit cooperation, affiliate transactions, and non-compete scope.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the indemnification cap, earnout mechanics, debt payoff requirements, environmental survival, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, R&W insurance waiver, non-compete scope, and closing conditions.

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the Environmental DD Summary dated October 18, 2025 as support for markup positions, including the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, environmental representation survival, government contract novation, and environmental permit cooperation.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties well over 8 of the 12 planted issues to specific SPA sections. Examples include MAE (§1.01), earnout (§2.05), government contracts (§§4.16, 6.05, 7.02), environmental survival (§9.01), affiliate transactions (§6.01), debt payoff (§§2.03, 2.08, 7.02), indemnification cap (§§1.01, 9.04), permit cooperation (§§4.15, 6.05), non-compete (§6.09), and sandbagging (§9.06).

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides draft-ready contract text for well over 8 of the 12 planted issues, including MAE, earnout, government contracts/novation, environmental survival, Dalton Creek indemnity, affiliate transactions, debt payoff, indemnification cap, permit cooperation, R&W insurance subrogation, non-compete, and sandbagging.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter discussion identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness: Cascade Mutual Bank's $28.0 million senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp.'s $9.8 million equipment financing, and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.'s $4.5 million subordinated seller note.
